# PHY abstraction


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A *PHY abstraction* gives the packet error rate of a transmission from
its SINR, without simulating its bits. An
[`ErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/phy_abstraction.html#errormodel)
does it for a batch of transmissions at once:

- [`BPSKErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/phy_abstraction.html#bpskerrormodel)
  (the default) uses uncoded BPSK over AWGN. Its bit error rate is
  `Q(√(2 SINR))`, with independent bit errors, so bigger packets fail
  more often.
- [`ThresholdErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/phy_abstraction.html#thresholderrormodel)
  receives a packet when the SINR is at or above a threshold.
- [`EESMErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/phy_abstraction.html#eesmerrormodel)
  combines the subcarriers by EESM, then applies a logistic packet-error
  curve with your calibration, e.g. a Wi-Fi MCS.
- [`SionnaErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/sionna_sys.html#sionnaerrormodel)
  (see `sionna_sys`) uses 5G NR with LDPC codes: Sionna SYS’s calibrated
  tables, the subcarriers combined by EESM, and link adaptation.

The two simple models use the mean SINR over the subcarriers. The
functions below are the analytic rates they use.

An
[`ErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/phy_abstraction.html#errormodel)
is a block: called with the SINR of a step’s transmissions at each
subcarrier (`sinr`), their sizes (`size_bits`), their broadcasts
(`group`) and whether they are sent (`active`), it gives their packet
error rates (`per`), symbols on the air (`num_symbols`) and metadata
(`info`). It rates only the transmissions sent and not between nodes at
the same place (an infinite SINR, lost never), so a new model only
writes `rate`.

This is Sionna SYS’s `sionna.sys.phy_abstraction` (`PHYAbstraction`),
with its `sionna.sys.effective_sinr` (EESM). Sionna’s `PHYAbstraction`
also draws which blocks are decoded; here
[`Decide`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/phy_abstraction.html#decide)
does, so a model only gives rates.

```

    snr:float, # Linear signal-to-noise ratio

```

*Bit error rate of BPSK over AWGN: Q(sqrt(2 snr)).*

``` python
assert packet_error_rate(30, 1000) < 1e-6 and packet_error_rate(-5, 1000) > 0.99
assert packet_error_rate(4, 10) < packet_error_rate(4, 1000)                  # bigger packets fail more often
assert packet_error_rate(9, 100, 'threshold') == 1.0 and packet_error_rate(10, 100, 'threshold') == 0.0
assert packet_error_rate(-math.inf, 8) == 1.0 and packet_error_rate(math.inf, 8) == 0.0
```

### ErrorModel

``` python
class ErrorModel(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*A PHY abstraction: the packet error rate of transmissions, from their
SINR. Subclasses write `rate`.*

The copies of a broadcast are one emission: a model that picks a rate
(e.g. an MCS) gives them the same one.

### EESMErrorModel

``` python
class EESMErrorModel(
    beta:float, # EESM parameter of the MCS
    threshold_db:float, # Effective SINR at which a `reference_bytes` packet is lost 10% of the time
    slope:float=1.5, # Steepness of the waterfall (1/dB)
    reference_bytes:int=1000, # Packet size of `threshold_db`; other sizes scale as independent pieces
    bits_per_symbol:float=1.0, # For the symbols on the air (the latency of `SystemLevelChannel`)
):
```

*EESM over the subcarriers, then a logistic packet error rate: a PHY
abstraction calibrated by its parameters (e.g. a Wi-Fi MCS).*

### eesm

``` python
def eesm(
    sinr:np.ndarray, # Linear SINR at each subcarrier
    beta:float, # EESM parameter (of an MCS)
)->float:
```

*Effective SINR (linear) of SINRs at several subcarriers: -β
ln(mean(exp(-SINR/β))).*

``` python
wifi = EESMErrorModel(beta=28.0, threshold_db=21.0, slope=1.5)              # ~802.11ac MCS 7 (approximate)
per, _, info = wifi([np.full(52, 10 ** 2.1), np.full(52, 10 ** 2.6)], np.array([8000, 8000]))
assert abs(per[0] - 0.1) < 1e-9 and per[1] < 0.01 and abs(info[0]['sinr_eff_db'] - 21) < 1e-9   # 10% at the threshold
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
faded = 10 ** 2.1 * np.abs((rng.standard_normal(52) + 1j * rng.standard_normal(52)) / np.sqrt(2)) ** 2
assert eesm(faded, 28.0) < np.mean(faded)                                   # faded subcarriers count for more
assert wifi([np.zeros(52)], np.array([100]))[0][0] == 1.0
assert wifi([np.full(52, 10 ** 2.1)], np.array([16000]))[0][0] > per[0]     # bigger packets fail more
```

``` python
per, symbols, _ = BPSKErrorModel()([np.array([10 ** 0.6]), np.array([10 ** 0.2, 10.0])], np.array([100, 100]))
assert np.allclose(per, [packet_error_rate(6, 100), packet_error_rate(10 * np.log10((10 ** 0.2 + 10) / 2), 100)])
assert symbols.tolist() == [100, 100]
# as a block: the SINRs of a step, (n, K); not rated: the ones not sent, and nodes at the same place (never lost)
per, symbols, info = BPSKErrorModel()(np.array([[1.0], [math.inf], [1.0]]), np.array([10, 10, 0]), active=np.array([True, True, False]))
assert per[0] > 0 and per[1] == per[2] == 0 and symbols.tolist() == [10, 10, 0] and info == [{}, {}, {}]
assert ThresholdErrorModel(10)([np.array([9.9]), np.array([10.0])], np.array([8, 8]))[0].tolist() == [1.0, 0.0]
```

## What arrives

[`Decide`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/phy_abstraction.html#decide)
draws whether each packet arrives: it is lost with its packet error
rate. It draws once per transmission sent, from its own generator
(`reset(seed)` makes it reproducible).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh/comm-core/blob/main/comm_core/phy_abstraction.py#L154"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Decide

``` python
class Decide(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*Whether each packet arrives: lost with its packet error rate, one draw
per transmission sent.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh/comm-core/blob/main/comm_core/phy_abstraction.py#L159"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Decide.call

``` python
def call(
    per:np.ndarray, # Packet error rate of each transmission
    active:np.ndarray | None=None, # Whether each one is sent (None: all)
)->np.ndarray:
```

*The block’s work: its inputs -\> its outputs (one value, a tuple in the
order of `outputs`, or a dict by name).*

``` python
d = Decide()
d.reset(seed=0); first = d(np.full(2000, 0.3))
assert abs(1 - first.mean() - 0.3) < 0.03                              # lost 30% of the time
d.reset(seed=0); assert (d(np.full(2000, 0.3)) == first).all()          # reproducible
assert d(np.array([0.0, 0.0]), active=np.array([True, False])).tolist() == [True, False]   # not sent: not arrived
```
